rows.name: TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES
rows.values: Comma-separated entries with no spaces. Each entry is `+name` (record) or `-name` (do not record). `name` is a trace category, or the start of one followed by `*`.
rows.default: Unset: no selection. Perfetto records every category except those tagged `slow` or `debug` (`driver-detail` and `memory`). An empty value counts as unset.
rows.effect: Selects the trace categories (named groups of Perfetto events) that an in-process trace records. The process writes an in-process trace to a file itself. That covers `runtron --trace FILE`, `runtron --trace-gen FILE`, a SIGUSR1 capture when `TRACE_FILE` names a file, and a FUSE capture that names no categories.
rows.notes: A bad entry fails the trace start. Any non-empty value fails a trace that goes to `traced` (the Perfetto daemon). A SIGUSR1 capture goes there when `TRACE_FILE` is unset. A failed start ends the process. A FUSE capture is the exception: it reports the error.

evidence.quote: if (const char* spec = trace_categories_spec()) categories = spec;

rows.name: TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN
rows.values: Integer count of tokens, parsed with `atoi`. A negative number counts as `0`. Text that is not a number counts as `0`.
rows.default: Unset: `0` tokens. The trace starts when prompt parsing completes.
rows.effect: With `runtron --trace-gen FILE`, the trace starts when the prompt tokens plus the generated tokens of a request reach the value. A value at or below the prompt length starts the trace when prompt parsing completes.
rows.notes: Only `--trace-gen` without `--trace-passes` uses the value. `--trace` ignores it. With `--trace-passes`, runtron logs the warning `--trace-passes overrides TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN`. If no request reaches the value, the trace starts and ends when the first request finishes. The value is read once per process.

rows.name: TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR
rows.values: The exact text `1` selects the arena allocator (`pos_heap_v2`). Any other text selects the legacy allocator (`pos_heap`). That includes `0`, `true` and an empty value.
rows.default: Unset: the build default applies. The CMake option `TRON_ARENA_ALLOCATOR_DEFAULT_ON` is `ON` by default. That selects the arena allocator. Empty: the legacy allocator.
rows.effect: Selects the allocator of the DMA heap (the hugepage memory that the programs allocate FPGA buffers from). With the arena allocator, KV cache entries are removed when hugepage use passes a target. The FUSE stats files under `/rinzler/stats/dma_heap/` exist only with the arena allocator.
rows.notes: No command-line flag selects the allocator. The arena allocator ignores `RZ_KV_CACHE_GB`, `--kv-cache-gb` and `--kv-cache-bytes`, and logs a warning for each one supplied. `TRON_HEAP_SHADOW` needs the arena allocator. Check: the log line `pos_heap_setup: using arena allocator (pos_heap_v2)`. The legacy allocator logs no line.

evidence.quote: option(TRON_ARENA_ALLOCATOR_DEFAULT_ON "Use pos_heap_v2 as the default DMA allocator" ON)

rows.name: TRON_USE_SPECULATION
rows.values: Integer, parsed with `atoi`. Any result other than `0` turns it on. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. `true` leaves it off.
rows.effect: For each loaded model, the scheduler looks for a built-in EAGLE draft model (a small model that proposes tokens for the main model to check). The name is `eagle-<model id>`, also tried without `-good`, `-fast`, `-nice` and `-best`. If one exists, it is loaded and rinzler generates with speculative decoding.
rows.notes: With a draft model, rinzler answers HTTP 400 to requests for logprobs (non-gemma models), structured output, tool calling or `reasoning_budget_tokens`. Missing draft weights stop the process. runtron uses the draft model only with `--draft-model`. Check: the log line `Found EAGLE model for <model>: <eagle model>`.

evidence.quote: return env ? std::atoi(env) : false;  // Disabled by default.

rows.name: TZ
rows.read_by: The C library, through `localtime_r` and `mktime` calls in `rinzler` and `rinzler_proxy` (`src/rinzler/harmony.cpp`, `rust/minijinja/src/lib.rs`). TRON code does not call `getenv` for it.
rows.values: A time zone setting that the C library parses. TRON code does not parse it.
rows.default: Unset: the C library chooses the time zone. TRON code has no rule for this case.
rows.effect: Sets the time zone of the local date and time that rinzler writes into prompts. This affects `conversation_start_date` in the system message of `gpt-oss` models, the output of `strftime_now` in chat templates, and the `rendered_at` field of a `save_tokens` capture.
rows.notes: `RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE` pins the date. The current time is then not used, and the pinned date is taken as local noon. A code comment says that glibc reads `TZ` only once. Set it before the process starts. The `rendered_at` field shows the date in effect.

rows.name: USE_HW_ATTN
rows.values: Integer `N`, parsed with `atol`. `N` of `0` or less turns hardware attention off. `N` above `0` turns it on. Text that is not a number counts as `0`.
rows.default: Unset: on from token position 127 for models generated by ingest, off for other models. Empty: off for every model.
rows.effect: Chooses hardware attention or software attention for every eligible model. `N` above `0` also sets the first token position that hardware attention serves. That position is the smallest value `k*128 - 1` that is not below `N`: `1` gives position 127, `128` gives position 255.
rows.notes: No command-line flag sets it. `true` and `on` count as `0` and turn it off. A model or server without hardware attention support stays on software attention. Check: the log lines `HW attention enabled for model` (field `engagement=`) and `HW attention disabled for model`.

evidence.quote: //   - USE_HW_ATTN unset defaults to enabled for *ingested* models, disabled for others

rows.name: USE_PYTHON_TOKENIZER
rows.values: Any text other than the exact text `false` turns it on. The comparison is case-sensitive. `0`, `False` and an empty value turn it on.
rows.default: Unset: the Rust tokenizer is used when the model directory holds `tokenizer.json`. Otherwise the Python tokenizer is used. Empty: on.
rows.effect: Forces the Python tokenizer (a helper program that runs as a child process) in place of the Rust tokenizer (the Hugging Face library inside the process). The helper program runs once to load the vocabulary and once for every encode call.
rows.notes: When `VALIDATE_TOKENIZERS` is on, this variable is ignored. `TRON_TOKENIZE_PY` names the helper program. The process stops when the helper program does not exist. rinzler ignores it for models whose id contains `gpt-oss`. The Python tokenizer logs the warning `Falling back to slow tokenizer script <program>`.

evidence.quote: spdlog::warn("Falling back to slow tokenizer script {}", program.string());

rows.name: VALIDATE_TOKENIZERS
rows.values: Any text other than the exact text `false` turns it on. The comparison is case-sensitive. `0`, `False` and an empty value turn it on.
rows.default: Unset: no validation. One tokenizer is created. Empty: on.
rows.effect: Creates the Rust tokenizer and the Python tokenizer for each model directory. Each encode and decode call runs both, logs any mismatch as an error and returns the Python result. Where encode adds begin-of-sequence or end-of-sequence tokens, it uses ids that this mode picks itself and does not apply `add_bos_token`.
rows.notes: Overrides `USE_PYTHON_TOKENIZER`. Needs the Python helper program (`TRON_TOKENIZE_PY`). The process stops when the Python tokenizer cannot be created. Every encode call starts a Python child process. rinzler ignores it for `gpt-oss` models. Check: the log line `Using validation tokenizer to compare Rust and Python implementations`.

evidence.quote: spdlog::error("Core tokenization mismatch for text: {}", sv);

new_terms.definition: A named group of Perfetto trace events. The registered names are `rinzler`, `sys`, `scheduler`, `model`, `model-moe`, `matmul`, `loading`, `driver`, `driver-detail`, `gen`, `hwattention`, `hwattention-detail`, `hw` and `memory`.
A Perfetto trace that the process writes to a file itself. The other kind is a trace that `traced` collects.
The Perfetto daemon. It collects a trace with the categories of its own config file.
A trace of 10 seconds that rinzler or runtron starts when it receives the signal SIGUSR1.
An in-process trace that a running rinzler records on request, through files in its FUSE stats mount.
The hugepage memory that the programs allocate FPGA buffers from.
The two allocators of the DMA heap: `pos_heap_v2` (arena) and `pos_heap` (legacy).
A small model that proposes next tokens. The main model then checks them. This method is called speculative decoding.

The two tokenizer implementations. The Rust tokenizer is the Hugging Face library inside the process, and it reads `tokenizer.json`. The Python tokenizer is a helper program that runs as a child process.

notes: All 8 rows checked against the code at commit 7eddde7895. No row dropped, none missing. Meaning changed in 4 rows. (1) TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES: a failed trace start ends runtron too, not only a process in a SIGUSR1 capture. (2) TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN: a value that no request reaches gives a trace that starts and ends when the first request finishes. (3) TRON_USE_SPECULATION: the draft model name is also tried with -good, -fast, -nice and -best removed, and missing draft weights stop the process. (4) VALIDATE_TOKENIZERS: rinzler ignores it for gpt-oss models. Wording only in TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR (effect) and TZ (read_by). USE_HW_ATTN and USE_PYTHON_TOKENIZER are unchanged. Confirmed writer choices: rinzler_proxy is left out of read_by for TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES (no FUSE mount, no SIGUSR1 tracer in the fake device library) and for TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR (pos_heap_setup is never called). USE_PYTHON_TOKENIZER stays for developers: README.tokenizers.md recommends the Rust tokenizer for production and the helper program defaults to a path in the source tree. Facts left out for lack of room: USE_HW_ATTN values above 2^30 are capped. The log line `HW attention disabled` prints the fixed reason `USE_HW_ATTN=0` for every value that turns it off. The Python tokenizer reports no special-token list, so rinzler disables the ATEM protocol and answers HTTP 400 to `reasoning_budget_message` requests. A process that serves a pipeline stage rejects a config with a draft model (`EAGLE speculation does not support pipeline stages`). The tool perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh refuses a rinzler that has TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES set. TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES evidence does not include the source of the default rule: h/common/perfetto.hpp:249 (comment) with the tags at :122 and :138. Evidence quotes are the source lines without their leading indentation.
